sngl:ui/markup

sngl:ui/markup Inline rich text: the `span` family, and the `richText` node that shows a run of it. A component joins the family by naming that tree in its return position. The family is inline and nothing else — emphasis, a link, a piece of code inside a sentence — because inline is the part of a document that has no other way to be said. A heading is a `text` with a size, a quote is a `vbox` with a rule down its left edge, a list is a `vbox` of rows; all three are ordinary layout, already implemented on every platform, and a markup component for each would be a construct five platforms reimplement to reach what `sngl:ui` hands them. A bold word inside a sentence is not: it has to live inside one flow of text with the words around it, and a box cannot hold it without breaking the line. So a document is a `vbox` of `richText` runs interleaved with whatever else the document holds — a code sample, a table, a chart — and each `richText` is one flow. That is also what makes a document extensible: a thing this package cannot express is a `ui.node` placed between two runs rather than a gap in the vocabulary. Text in the family is literal. A space is a space and a newline ends the line, whatever the target, so a run written here renders as it was written and a platform that collapses whitespace is the one that has to stop. That is why there is no line-break component: `"\n"` is one, and a second spelling of it would be a second answer to give. Components
  • bold The word carries weight.
  • caption A caption: what the thing above or below it is.
  • codeBlock A code sample on its own, as opposed to a `monospace` run inside a sentence.
  • heading1 A document's own title -- the one heading a page has at most one of.
  • heading2 A section title.
  • heading3 A subsection title.
  • heading4 A title below a subsection.
  • heading5 A title four levels down; rare outside a reference document.
  • heading6 The deepest title a document outline has.
  • image A picture on the line with the words -- an icon, a badge, an inline formula -- from any source a `ui.image` takes.
  • italic The word is slanted, using the family's italic face where one exists.
  • link The words lead somewhere.
  • list A list, and one item of one.
  • listItem One item.
  • monospace A run set in a monospaced face -- an identifier, a flag, a filename, a line of a code sample.
  • paragraph A run of prose -- the block a paragraph of a document becomes, and the default.
  • quote Words quoted from somewhere else.
  • richText Shows one flow of rich text.
  • run A run of text and what is true of its appearance -- the one span that carries style, and what every wrapper below is written in terms of.
  • span The tree the inline pieces form.
  • strike A rule through the words: text that was there and is not any more.
  • text A literal run of text -- the leaf every other span eventually holds.
  • token The content is a run of code of this kind.
  • underline A rule under the words.
    • Types
  • Palette A color per `Token` kind.
  • SpanStyle What an inline run may vary about its own appearance.
    • Enums
  • Role What a run of text is *for*, as opposed to what it looks like.
  • Slant Slant of a run, with `inherit` first for the same reason.
  • Task Whether a list item is a task, and if so whether it is done.
  • Token What a run of code *is*, for a platform to color as it sees fit.
  • Weight Weight of a run, with `inherit` first so an unset one leaves its parent's alone.
    • Functions
  • bulletAt The bullet for a nesting level.
  • colorOf The color `kind` is drawn in: the palette's where it sets one, and the fallback's where it does not.
  • tokenColor The color a palette gives one kind.
    • Constants
  • bullets The bullets, cycling by depth the way a document does: a nested list wants to look different from the one it sits in, and after three levels the eye has stopped counting anyway.
  • darkPalette
  • lightPalette GitHub's syntax colors, light and dark: what a platform with no theme of its own to ask draws code in.
